Earned score

.dr-listing__score · components/card.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Olena H.· 5.0

“Fast and careful — package arrived sealed and on time.”

Package deliveryToday
  1. 1.dr-listing__nameThe name the score belongs to; the score rides inside it, on its line.
  2. 2.dr-listing__scoreThe suffix: 12.5/400 in --text-muted, 5.95:1 on the card, tabular figures, 8 from the name.
  3. 3.dr-listing__metaThe review's service and date, as chips under the quote.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: (.dr-listing__score, .dr-stars).

When to use

The earned score is a score somebody else gave, not a score being given. On ratings it sits beside each reviewer's name as · 5.0, written as a number rather than drawn as stars, so it cannot be read as a control. .dr-rating is an input: five buttons, each a 44pt target with aria-pressed, for rate, where the client awards a score. A display must not be a row of buttons announcing a pressed state it cannot change (WCAG 4.1.2), nor put five stops in a dashboard's tab order.

The read-only star row DESIGN.md names .dr-stars is not declared in components/. The overall rating on ratings is drawn instead by the balance block: the .dr-rating-arc mask over the figure, aria-hidden, with the figure stating the value.

The value is written with one decimal and a middle dot, · 4.0, never as a sentence and never with a star glyph the user might tap.

Sources: DESIGN.md § The earned score · inventory.md § 1 · ui/kit.html § Earned score

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Andriy P.· 4.0

“Good shots overall, a couple came out a bit dark.”

Photo & videoYesterday

A review card on ratings: the score as a muted suffix on the reviewer's name, the review under it.

Don’t

The rating input used to show a score already given: five buttons announcing a pressed state the reader cannot change. Show a received score as .dr-listing__score, or as the figure of a balance block when it is the screen's headline.
